I am 63 years old and have been farming these small plots all my life. This piece of land is only 0.15 hectares and I grow beans here, mostly intercropped with a little maize. Beans do not need chemical fertilizer—they fix their own nitrogen from the air—and at my age with no schooling, I do not have money to buy inputs for a small legume plot when my family needs to eat. My children and grandchildren will help me with the planting, weeding, and harvesting, but there is no reason to hire ganyu workers for such a small piece, and the rains in Mulanje have always been enough without irrigation.
